newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares down at Tuesday's Christmas break.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares down at Tuesday's Christmas break.

text.p: The party mood in Singapore dealing rooms as brokers counted down the hours to the lunchtime Christmas close on Tuesday did not filter through to share prices, which ended the day down.
At the early Christmas close at 0430 GMT for the Singapore stock market, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was down 8.72 points at 2,187.14.
Dealers said they expected prices to be weaker before picking up again in January after the Singapore general election, now confirmed for January 2.
"But we may pick up a little before then," one dealer said.
The fall on the STII was mirrored by a drop on the Business Times-Singapore Regional Index of 1.94 points to 1,084.47.
Total traded volume was a paltry 46.2 million shares, with losers just ahead of gainers at 114 to 107.
The star shining at the top of the Christmas gainers' tree was OUB Bank's foreign tranche, up Singapore $0.30 to S$10.70.
The day's largest loser was port services company China Merchants, down Hong Kong $0.80 at HK$4.40.
Singapore's stock market closed at 0430 GMT and will reopen at 0100 GMT on Thursday, December 26.
